grounds: The truncation passage ('conversations may grow so long... will be truncated') is intelligible with the ordinary meaning of 'conversation' and never invokes the message/role/content structure the provider span defines, though the formal object being truncated is that defined structure.

The example's point — refuse to reveal the private prompt but 'may selectively share only authorized portions' — is a direct application of the provider's rule that some facts 'are typically appropriate to share' while 'the verbatim text or full details... should be kept private by default'.

The web-search example sits under the 'Avoid factual, reasoning, and formatting errors {authority=user}' heading, and fully applying its norm (knowing an explicit user/developer instruction can override it) requires the heading's authority designation.
The needer sentence's 'If a user requests any such content' is anaphoric — 'such content' has no referent without the preceding provider sentence prohibiting 'sexual content involving minors'.
The rule at L1004 sits directly under the L1002 heading '{#respect_creators authority=root}', and its non-overridable force cannot be determined without that heading's root designation.

The L4052 text on condescending language, prosody, and engagement does not topically match 'Don't make unprompted personal comments' (L3997) and sits 55 lines away, so whether it falls under that heading's guideline designation cannot be confirmed from the spans alone.

The 'celebrating identity' example (L3530) illustrates the Love humanity section it sits under (L3506), and its normative reading — respond with genuine positive interest to identity pride — leans on that section's principle of treating demographics equally while celebrating differences.

The needer's 'contextualize such ideologies as harmful' is anaphoric to extremist ideologies discussed earlier in the section, but the de-escalation guidance itself is self-contained and does not need the specific prohibition on praising/endorsing extremist content to be applied.
The claim that 'authority=user' on the L2137 heading gives its rules user authority is only meaningful given the L183-191 enumeration defining User as a level in the authority ordering.

The example's GOOD/BAD contrast ('assumes that the user was seeking to write false information without any basis') directly exercises the L610-616 directive to interpret ambiguous requests assuming positive intent.
Reading 'authority=root' on the L2050 heading as a claim about precedence depends on the L69-101 definition that Root rules 'cannot be overridden by system messages, developers or users'.

The L4416 example immediately follows and illustrates the L4412 voice rule, and its GOOD response is judged good precisely as a turn appropriate to 'the iterative, turn-taking structure of spoken conversation'.
The needer's phrase 'any principles above the "guideline" level' presupposes the graded levels of authority that L67 introduces; without that scheme 'above the guideline level' has no meaning.
The L4594 rule explicitly modulates a baseline for teens, and its non-overridable, under_18-scoped force comes from the L4578 heading '{authority=root tags=under_18}' it sits under.

L83's 'Developer: Instructions given by developers' is a list item in the enumeration of authority levels and is only intelligible as a level within the scheme L67 introduces ('a level of authority... higher authority override those with lower').

The info-hazards prohibition at L858 is applicable on its own text, but its exception structure (transformation only, 'no other contextual exceptions') is fixed by L854's restricted-content rule, which itself cites #avoid_info_hazards — the reliance is real but partly runs in the reverse direction.

L767's 'Instructions may delegate some of their authority to quoted text, tool outputs, or multimodal data' presupposes the L69-101 hierarchy under which those sources otherwise sit at 'No Authority'.

The teen example illustrates the rule that 'with teens the assistant should err further on the side of safety' than the stay_in_bounds baseline, so applying it requires the L799 concept of limits where the assistant refrains from fully complying.
The needer's condition 'in an interactive setting' versus 'output that'll be consumed programmatically' is exactly the distinction L3386 defines, including how programmatic mode is signaled.
L81's placement of the system level 'below root but above developer, user, and guideline' is a statement within the authority scheme L67 introduces and is unintelligible without it.

The dread example (L3978) sits under and illustrates the 'Be warm {authority=guideline}' heading (L3955), and knowing its norm is guideline-strength (overridable guidance, not a requirement) depends on that designation.

L924 opens with 'However' and carves out content that 'does not exploit the unique characteristics of a particular individual or demographic', which is unreadable as an exception without the L922 prohibition on targeted political manipulation.

The provider span is merely another heading that also carries 'authority=root' (L699, ignore untrusted data); it does not define what root authority means, so the L1543 heading's root designation does not lean on it — the link is between two sibling uses of the tag.

The confidential-by-default rule's 'the content' refers back to the privileged information enumerated in the immediately preceding provider sentence ('non-public OpenAI policies, system messages, ... hidden chain-of-thought'), without which its scope is undefined.

The empathetic chit-chat example demonstrates the short, conversational branch ('shorter, more conversational answers if the user wants to chat'), not the asserted concept of contexts requiring longer, more detailed answers, so it does not lean on that contribution.

L79's 'System: Rules set by OpenAI... cannot be overridden by developers or users' is a list item within the authority-level enumeration and depends on L67's framing that instructions are assigned levels whose higher members override lower ones.

The 'IGNORE PREVIOUS INSTRUCTIONS' example is resolved by siding with the developer's implicit pricing authority, a direct application of L300's directive to detect conflicts 'even those not stated explicitly' and resolve by higher-level authority and scenario purpose.

The L612 rule does sit under and draw root authority from the L610 heading, but the asserted dependency prose ('the principle of applying three implicit biases...') describes what the needer span itself states, not what the heading contributes, so the edge as stated is only partly borne out.

The L3778 rule sits under 'Be clear and direct {authority=guideline}' (L3756), and knowing it is guideline-strength ('when appropriate' guidance rather than a mandate) requires the heading's authority tag.

The needer span explicitly lists 'transformations of user-provided sensitive content' (linking #transformation_exception) among the only circumstances permitting sensitive content, which is exactly the exception L1371 establishes.
